name: sol_defi_oracle_7
description: Missing staleness/heartbeat check on price oracle data, allowing use of stale prices
question: The source file in `source` retrieves a price from an oracle (e.g., via latestRoundData or a similar price-feed call) and uses that price in on-chain calculations without checking the returned update timestamp against any staleness threshold or heartbeat, so a stale or outdated price can be used, excluding code that compares the feed's updatedAt (or equivalent) timestamp against a defined maximum age before using the price.
criteria: Calls latestRoundData() (or equivalent) and immediately uses the returned price/answer in a calculation without reading or checking the updatedAt/timestamp field
Reads updatedAt from the oracle response but never compares it against any staleness threshold or heartbeat value before using the price
Caches or stores a previously fetched oracle price in a state variable and reuses it in later calculations with no check on how long ago it was last updated
Falls back to a hardcoded or previously stored price when the oracle call fails or reverts, and uses that fallback price in calculations without any freshness or timestamp validation
